{{nihongo|'''Tsutsumine Shrine'''|堤根神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

== Japanese content ==
{{出典の明記|date=2020年4月}}
'''Tsutsumine Shrine''' (つつみねじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kadoma, Osaka|ar|كادوما (أوساكا)|ban|Kadoma, Osaka|ca|Kadoma (Osaka)|ce|Кадома (Япон)|ceb|Kadoma (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Kadoma (Osaka)|eo|Kadoma|es|Kadoma (Osaka)|fa|کادوما، اوساکا|fi|Kadoma|fr|Kadoma (Osaka)|gl|Kadoma|id|Kadoma, Ōsaka|it|Kadoma (Giappone)|ja|門真市|ko|가도마시|lt|Kadoma (Japonija)|mzn|کادوما، اوساکا|nl|Kadoma (Japan)|no|Kadoma (Osaka)|pl|Kadoma (Japonia)|pt|Kadoma|ro|Kadoma, Japonia|ru|Кадома (Япония)|sh|Kadoma|sr|Кадома (Јапан)|sv|Kadoma, Osaka|tg|Кадома|th|คาโดมะ|tl|Kadoma, Osaka|tr|Kadoma, Japonya|tt|Кадома (Япония)|uk|Кадома|ur|کاڈوما، اوساکا|vi|Kadoma, Ōsaka|war|Kadoma, Osaka|zh|門真市|zh_classical|門眞市|zh_min_nan|Kadoma-chhī|zh_yue|門真|qid=Q496080}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It was founded as the guardian of {{ill|Mamuta Embankment|Q11617931|qid=Q11617931}}, and is a Shikinaisha listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}. However, there are two Tsutsumine Shrines in Kadoma, and both claim to be the Shikinaisha.

=== Tsutsumine Shrine (Miyanochō, Kadoma) ===

Tsutsumine Shrine in Miyanochō, Kadoma, stands along the former Manda no Tsutsumi on the south bank of the Furukawa, a tributary of the {{ill|Yodo River|Q1140505|qid=Q1140505}}. Its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

Its deities are {{ill|Hikoyai|ja|日子八井命|simple|Hikoyai|zh|彥八井耳命|qid=Q11086120|lt=Hiko-yaimimi-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}}. It is said the Manda clan, deeply connected to construction of {{ill|Mamuta Embankment|Q11617931|qid=Q11617931}}, enshrined their ancestral deity Hiko-yaimimi-no-Mikoto as guardian of the embankment.

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in the mid-Heian period, it was listed first among five shrines of Manda District, Kawachi Province, and was Kadoma's only {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. In front of the torii passed the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gyōki Road}}, linking {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi}} and {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato}}, and it drew worship from old times. In the {{ill|Kan'ei|es|Kan'ei|fa|کانئی|fr|Ère Kan'ei|id|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|ko|간에이|ru|Канъэй|simple|Kan'ei|sr|Канеи|sv|Kanei|tr|Kan'ei|zh|寬永|qid=Q1192913}} period (early Edo), local lord {{ill|Nagai Naomasa|Q6958349|qid=Q6958349}} (Nagai Shinano-no-kami Naomasa) merged worship of Kankō (Michizane), whom he revered, and thereafter it was called "Tenmangū." In Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|ab|1872|af|1872|als|1872|am|1872 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1872|ar|1872|ary|1872|arz|1872|ast|1872|avk|1872|az|1872|azb|۱۸۷۲ (میلادی)|ba|1872 йыл|ban|1872|bar|1872|bat_smg|1872|bcl|1872|be|1872|be_x_old|1872|bg|1872|bn|১৮৭২|bpy|মারি ১৮৭২|br|1872|bs|1872.|ca|1872|cdo|1872 nièng|ce|1872 шо|ceb|1872|ckb|١٨٧٢|crh|1872|cs|1872|csb|1872|cv|1872|cy|1872|da|1872|de|1872|diq|1872|el|1872|eml|1872|eo|1872|es|1872|et|1872|eu|1872|fa|۱۸۷۲|fi|1872|fiu_vro|1872|fo|1872|fr|1872|frp|1872|frr|1872|fur|1872|fy|1872|ga|1872|gan|1872年|gcr|1872|gd|1872|gl|1872|gv|1872|he|1872|hi|१८७२|hif|1872|hr|1872.|hsb|1872|ht|1872 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1872|hy|1872|hyw|1872 թուական|ia|1872|id|1872|ilo|1872|io|1872|is|1872|it|1872|ja|1872年|jv|1872|ka|1872|kaa|1872|kk|1872 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೨|ko|1872년|krc|1872 джыл|ku|1872|kv|1872-ӧд во|la|1872|lb|1872|lez|1872 йис|li|1872|lij|1872|lmo|1872|lt|1872 m.|lv|1872. gads|mai|१८७२|map_bms|1872|mdf|1872|mg|1872|mhr|1872|mi|1872|min|1872|mk|1872|mr|इ.स. १८७२|mrj|1872 и|ms|1872|my|၁၈၇၂|myv|1872 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۲|nah|1872|nap|1872|nds|1872|nds_nl|1872|new|ई सं १८७२|nl|1872|nn|1872|no|1872|nrm|1872|nso|1872|oc|1872|olo|1872|or|୧୮୭୨|os|1872-æм аз|pa|1872|pam|1872|pl|1872|pnb|1872|pt|1872|qu|1872|ro|1872|ru|1872 год|rue|1872|sa|१८७२|sah|1872|scn|1872|sd|1872ع|se|1872|sh|1872.|shn|1872|si|1872|simple|1872|sk|1872|sl|1872|smn|1872|sq|1872|sr|1872|stq|1872|su|1872|sv|1872|sw|1872|szl|1872|ta|1872|te|1872|tet|1872|tg|Соли 1872|th|พ.ศ. 2415|tk|1872|tl|1872|tly|1872|tr|1872|tt|1872 ел|udm|1872 ар|uk|1872|ur|1872ء|uz|1872|vec|1872|vi|1872|vls|1872|vo|1872|wa|1872|war|1872|xmf|1872|yi|1872|za|1872 nienz|zea|1872|zh|1872年|zh_classical|一八七二年|zh_min_nan|1872 nî|zh_yue|1872年|qid=Q7753}}), it was ranked as village shrine.

Part of Manda no Tsutsumi remains near the shrine buildings, with a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=camphor tree}} over 500 years old growing on top. Until early Shōwa, much longer sections of the embankment remained, but they were cut away by housing development. Through efforts of the shrine priest, part was preserved and designated on March 29, Shōwa 48 as the Osaka Prefecture historic site "Traditional Manda no Tsutsumi."

Its deities are {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Sumeōkami}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Kami}}, and Ōnamuchi-no-Kami ({{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944}}).

The founding date is unknown, but in the cadastral register of {{ill|Bunroku|ckb|بونرۆکو|es|Bunroku|fa|بونروکو|fr|Ère Bunroku|ia|Bunroku|id|Bunroku|ja|文禄|ko|분로쿠|ru|Бунроку|simple|Bunroku|sr|Бунроку|sv|Bunroku|tr|Bunroku|uk|Бунроку|zh|文禄|zh_yue|文祿|qid=Q1373039}} 3 ({{ill|1594|Q6777|qid=Q6777}}), it appears as "Sannō-gū" serving as ujigami of Hiejima and Kuwasai villages. The "Sannō" name is thought to derive from enshrining Ōnamuchi-no-Kami. In the register of {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 10 ({{ill|1725|Q6932|qid=Q6932}}), it appears as "Yatsurugi Daimyōjin," likely from enshrining Susanoo-no-Kami. A document from Genbun 3 ({{ill|1738|Q6996|qid=Q6996}}) says three seats were enshrined by adding Amaterasu. In the Meiji 12 "Kita-Kawachi District Shrine Property Register," the name appears as "Ryōmura Shrine," and the deity is one seat of Amaterasu. The name came from being ujigami of two villages.

In Meiji 41, it was renamed "Tsutsumine Shrine" as an alleged descendant of the Shikinaisha Tsutsumine Shrine. There is no material proving Shikinaisha status, and it is thought the claim was made to avoid {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700}}, then actively promoted at the time; nevertheless, in August of that year it was merged into gōsha {{ill|Mishima Shrine (Taito)|Q11355275|qid=Q11355275}} (present 1374 Mitsushima, Kadoma). In Shōwa 21, it separated from Mishima Shrine and was restored at the old site.
